title: The Hero
text: What's up, Doc? How are you feeling, Private? Like I just stepped on a landmine. That's because you did. What's the damage? You lost a leg. That's the worst of it. My ears are still ringing. Any questions I might be able to answer? Yeah, I'm having a little trouble moving my left arm, Doc. That's because it's gone, Private. But you said the leg was the worst of it. Well, it is. A leg is bigger than an arm. A leg keeps you up, lets you walk and kick things. An arm is just for clapping, and there's no clapping on it. There's no entertainment. So the leg and the arm are the very worst of it? I would say the leg is the worst of it. Oh, Doctor, what about the rest of me? I still say the leg. Leg lets you sneak up on enemy. You could tiptoe, things like that. I can't feel anything below my neck, Doc. That's because it's gone, Private. It's all gone. It's just blown clear away. You're a mighty lucky man to still be alive. You mean I'm just a head? Well, sort of. You're also missing the back of your head. Oh, so I'm just a face, more or less? Yes, more or less, Private. That's not good. No, it's not, but I'm still sticking with the leg. You know, I've always been a big leg man. You ever see the stems on Betty Grable? Oh. Oh. Cigarette? Sure. Light? Yeah. Hold it for you? No. Yeah, all right. All right. What about the rest of the platoon? Monaghan? Dead. Douglas? Dead. Murphy? Dead. Hartford? Connecticut. Garrett? No. No. No. No. No. No. No. Dead. Hollywood? California. Went back yesterday. Well, I'm going to make the rounds, Private. If you need anything, just get up and... Oh. Well, if you need anything, just whistle. Thanks, Doc. How are you feeling, soldier? I know things look pretty bleak, but believe me, they could be a lot worse.
